text:
Maya: FYI — overnight perf sweep against paged-attn variant produced intermittent NaNs and huge tail latency on fp16 on prod cluster node-7. Attaching short summary from the profiler.
Chris: link? where are the traces?
Maya: perf-bot uploaded nvprof trace + cupy logs: https://internal-storage/runs/2199/trace-2199012345
perf-bot: nightly run 2026-03-17 03:12 UTC — job=paged-attn-sweep, model=gpt2x, dtype=fp16, batch policy=auto-batch-2, observed: 3 NaN events, 1 kernel retry (fallback to slower path), tail latency 3.2x baseline
Sam: quick read: looking at the NVTX it spikes inside the attention softmax kernel during long sequences (>1536). GPU util fine but error counters show fp16 exp overflow on some heads.
Elin: can you paste the offending kernel log block? even a snippet helps.
Maya: yes — from kernel stderr:
```
attn_softmax_kernel.cu: line 412: compute_expsum -> INF encountered
head 3: exp input 88.2
head 7: exp input 95.6
Result: NaN written to output
```
Tej: 88-95 for exp(input) is definitely going to overflow in fp16. We should clamp logits or use a log-sum-exp stable path. Was this kernel using the fast fused exp path? (i.e., no logsumexp normalization)
Chris: the paged flash variant we shipped last month swapped in an aggressive fused exp kernel for perf. It skips the double reduction and uses per-block approximate max. That probably removed the explicit log-sum-exp stabilization in the hot path.
Sam: hypothesis: the approximate max sometimes underestimates leading to large positive inputs to exp() in fp16, causing INF and NaN. It doesn't show up in bf16 builds because exponent range is larger.
Elin: repro steps requested — I'll try a small script that reproduces on a dev GPU. Can someone post the exact test command used by the sweep?
Maya: command used:
```
./bench_attn --model gpt2x --attn paged_flash --dtype fp16 --batch 4 --seq 2048 --kv-cache enabled --warmup 100 --iter 500 --profile nvtx
```
Tej: thanks. Quick mitigation ideas:
- revert to the safer softmax kernel for fp16 (slower but stable)
- add per-head scaling: subtract head_max before exp (explicit log-sum-exp)
- clamp logits to <= 30 or 50 as a stopgap
- enable mixed bf16 accumulation just for softmax
Any preference for quick rollback vs patch?
Maya: ops wants a hotfix if possible, rollback is easiest.
ops-bot: deploy bot: rolling canary to prod node pool 'paged-attn' scheduled at 2026-03-17T12:00Z if approved.
Chris: I can put a kernel selector gate: if dtype==fp16 and seq>1024 and max_logit_guess>35 then pick stable_softmax kernel. Fast to land.
Sam: minor note — we need to compute max_logit_guess cheaply; use block-level running max estimate from first pass or peek top-k per block. Keep cost <1%.
Elin: I'll prototype a guard: do a single reduction to compute per-head max (int8-ish pass) then switch kernels. If the max < 30, use fast fused path; else fallback.
Tej: for long-term: maybe implement a numerically-stable fused path that uses exp(x - max) internally rather than relying on approximate max. Harder but better.
Maya: can we add a perf test that exercises this guard so CI catches regressions? Currently our nightly sweep didn't trigger until prod because of seq/batch distribution.
Chris: add a unit perf test with seq=2048, batch=4, dtype=fp16 in perf-ci. Also add checks for NaNs in kernel outputs and regression alert if detected.
Sam: I ran a quick local repro. With clamp to 40 the NaNs disappear, tail latency rises ~5% only. Using stable_softmax fallback increases latency ~20% on that config.
Elin: patch idea submitted: PR#8421 — kernel-selector + clamp=40 by default for fp16. Requesting review from Tej & Chris.
Tej: reviewing now. Also add a comment documenting why clamp exists and link to profiler trace.
Maya: thanks. After merge let's run a canary and then schedule a broader rollout. Also add an alert in console: "attn-softmax-numeric-guardrail" whenever NaNs detected.
perf-bot: note: add perf regression gates — if fallback rate > 1% for any kernel path, notify eng-runtime and SRE.
Chris: sounds good. Post-mortem: feature that inlined the fast exp removed a stabilization step. Lesson: any kernel optimization that changes arithmetic order needs numeric-safety tests for edge cases (long sequences, fp16 extremes, kv-coldstart).
